atoms.sound: The French phrase à propos means by the way or talking of in English.
atoms.b: The French phrase “à propos” ((means)) “by the way” or “talking of” in English.

atoms.sound: What I meant was that not every rectangle is a square, but every square is a rectangle.
atoms.b: What I ((meant)) was that not every rectangle is a square, but every square is a rectangle.

atoms.sound: My present to you has meant that I really appreciate our friendship.

atoms.sound: Myra usually spends her summer holiday at a camp.
atoms.b: Myra usually ((spends)) her summer holiday at a camp.

atoms.sound: However, the last summer holiday she ((spent)) at her grandparents.
atoms.b: However, the last summer holiday she ((spent)) at her grandparents.

atoms.sound: Nonetheless, she wasn't at all sad that she hasn't spent the last summer at camp.
atoms.b: Nonetheless, she wasn't at all sad that she hasn't ((spent)) the last summer at camp.

atoms.sound: Timmy doesn't like to wear pants.
Even when he was still a little boy, he always wore skirts and dresses.

atoms.sound: The first time that he had worn a dress, his mother told him that he looked very good in it.

atoms.sound: I wonder what other subjects she has already taught before.
